VERDICT: EXTEND C0031 | `_count_tool_issues()` collapsing any runner exception to `0` does more than hide crashes. It also makes missing/timeouted/unparseable tools look identical to a clean file during `evaluate_fix()`. Downstream, `_compute_fix_verdict()` can mark a fix SAFE/NEUTRAL because both pre_* and new_* counts are spuriously zero, which can incorrectly set `finding.verified=True` in `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` Stage 4 and prematurely close the bug via NK bug-closed dedup on later rounds.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox tests against the patched source tree; it only writes a single patched file into a temp directory and then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir`. Evidence: in `evaluate_fix`, only `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))` is created. No package tree or sibling modules are copied. The optional tests are then executed via `_run_tool(test_cmd, ..., cwd=tmpdir)`. Any realistic command like the one used by `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` — `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]` — runs from a temp dir that does not contain `bench/tests/` or the rest of the package. Even if tests import `bench.*` from the original repo via ambient `PYTHONPATH` / current installation, they will exercise the original source, not the patched file, because the patched file is isolated as a basename-only file outside the package path.
FOLLOW: The claimed “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature can report misleading verdicts on the happy path. A fix that breaks imports, package wiring, or interactions with neighboring modules can still be labeled SAFE/NEUTRAL because static checks run only on the standalone patched file and tests either fail to locate the suite, run against the unmodified real package, or miss the patched module entirely. Downstream consequences: (1) `immune_agents` Stage 4 may set `verified=True` for an untested or wrongly tested fix; (2) NK duplicate handling can then close later findings as “bug closed”; (3) human reviewers receive a false signal that programmatic verification succeeded. This directly affects end-to-end correctness of the endocrine layer’s key new capability.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — in `evaluate_fix()`, copy the entire relevant source tree into `tmpdir` preserving relative paths, write the patch at the same relative location inside that sandbox, and run both static tools and `test_cmd` against that sandboxed tree (e.g. with `cwd=tmpdir` and sandbox-relative test paths / `PYTHONPATH=tmpdir`). Do not evaluate fixes against a lone basename file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` uses the sum of net issue deltas across tools (`total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`) to decide HARMFUL/SAFE. This permits issue cancellation: a fix that introduces new Bandit or type errors can still be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL if it removes more Ruff findings, because only the arithmetic sum is checked. Evidence: `_compute_fix_verdict` returns HARMFUL only when `total_net > 0`; if one tool worsens by +1 and another improves by -2, `total_net < 0` and the verdict becomes SAFE despite introducing a new issue class.
FOLLOW: This violates the module’s documented rule “SAFE: no new issues introduced”. Downstream, a fix that adds a security or type regression while cleaning up style can be marked SAFE, then `immune_agents` Stage 4 will set `finding.verified=True`. Once verified, later duplicate findings can be suppressed as bug-closed. This is silently wrong, not cosmetic, because a harmful fix is promoted into canonical closure state.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net metric is positive (`net_type_errors > 0 or net_ruff_errors > 0 or net_bandit_issues > 0`) before considering aggregate improvement. Only return SAFE when no metric worsened and at least one improved, or tests passed with all nets exactly zero.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the health scan advertises “pyright/ruff/bandit” static analysis between rounds, but `scan_health()` also runs `mypy` unconditionally and exposes its diagnostics in totals. This creates an interface mismatch with the documented endocrine contract and with downstream interpretation of health metrics. Evidence: module header and “The endocrine layer provides” list mention pyright/ruff/bandit; `scan_health()` iterates over `("pyright", "ruff", "bandit", "mypy")`.
FOLLOW: This is not just documentation drift. Health totals, counts_by_tool, counts_by_severity, and counts_by_category are inflated by an extra checker that the rest of the system is not told to expect. Pacing or human review based on “health scan” can interpret increased errors as regressions from the promised three-tool baseline. The same inconsistency affects fix evaluation, where pre/post type counts use pyright only, while health scan type counts include both pyright and mypy; the two endocrine outputs become incomparable.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make the contract consistent by either removing mypy from `scan_health()` for the PoC, or updating the public endocrine interface/docstrings to explicitly state that mypy is part of the health scan and fix-evaluation metrics. The simpler sufficient fix is to remove mypy from `scan_health()` until it is an intentional surfaced feature.
VERIFIED: TRUE
